stories.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection
stories.abstract: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog: a command injection flaw in UnrealIRCd and a permission assignment issue affecting various Check Point products. Both are currently being leveraged by threat actors in active cyberattacks.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing a high risk of unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.action: Update UnrealIRCd and affected Check Point products to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: FBI flash alert says Artex tool automating cyberattacks at ‘machine speed’
stories.abstract: The FBI reports that threat actors are leveraging ARTEX, an AI-driven penetration testing framework, to accelerate cyberattacks. The tool automates the chaining of exploits, enabling attackers to move from initial reconnaissance to administrative access in less than three hours.
stories.why: This framework lowers the barrier to entry for complex attacks, allowing adversaries to rapidly compromise cloud environments like Microsoft 365.

stories.title: Check Point security advisory (AV26-1154) – Update 1
stories.abstract: Check Point has disclosed two vulnerabilities affecting various products, including Force Firewalls and Management Servers. One of these flaws, CVE-2026-123039, is currently under active exploitation and has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: Active exploitation of perimeter security infrastructure poses a critical risk to network integrity and administrative access control.
stories.action: Review Check Point security advisories and apply available patches immediately.

stories.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808
stories.abstract: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices are vulnerable to critical remote code execution flaws, collectively dubbed php2shell, stemming from the underlying PHP runtime. These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated attackers to compromise affected hardware, which is widely deployed across critical manufacturing sectors.
stories.why: These critical RCE vulnerabilities carry a CVSS score of 9.8 and are actively exploited, posing a severe risk to industrial control systems.
stories.action: Restrict network access to affected devices and implement vendor-provided security configurations immediately.

stories.title: Siemens Desigo, Gridscale
stories.abstract: A critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability, dubbed Node2Shell, affects the Brotli decoder in various Siemens industrial products, including Desigo, Gridscale, and RUGGEDCOM. Exploitation could allow remote attackers to corrupt memory and execute arbitrary code.
stories.why: This high-severity flaw impacts critical infrastructure and industrial control systems, posing significant risks for remote code execution in operational technology environments.
stories.action: Update Siemens Desigo, Gridscale, and RUGGEDCOM software to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Flaws Actively Exploited Despite Available Patches
stories.abstract: CISA has added CVE-2026-20320, an XML external entity vulnerability affecting Cisco BroadWorks and other products, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw is currently being actively exploited in the wild, necessitating immediate attention for affected infrastructure.
stories.why: Active exploitation of this vulnerability in critical Cisco infrastructure poses a significant risk of unauthorized data access or system compromise.
stories.action: Update Cisco BroadWorks and Crosswork components to the versions specified in the Cisco security advisory.

stories.title: Google security advisory (AV26-1157)
stories.abstract: Google has released security updates for Chrome to address a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-125350, which is currently being exploited in the wild. The flaw affects Windows, Mac, and Linux versions of the browser.
stories.why: This vulnerability is confirmed to be under active exploitation and has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 157.0.8103.78 or later immediately.

stories.title: Exploit Attempts for GPUStack Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-102895), (Thu, Nov 12th)
stories.abstract: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-102895, affects GPUStack versions prior to 2.2.0. The flaw allows unauthorized access to systems managing GPU clusters, which are frequently utilized for high-value AI infrastructure and model training workloads.
stories.why: GPUStack manages high-compute resources; unauthorized access could lead to cryptojacking, data exfiltration, or the compromise of sensitive AI model weights.
stories.action: Update GPUStack to version 2.2.0 or later immediately.

stories.title: Barracuda Networks security advisory (AV26-1112) – Update 2
stories.abstract: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities affecting multiple Barracuda products, including Email Security Gateway and Web Application Firewall, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Evidence suggests that at least one of these flaws is currently being leveraged in active cyberattacks.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing a significant risk of unauthorized access or compromise to Barracuda infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Barracuda appliances to the latest firmware versions specified in the security advisory immediately.

stories.title: SCKit Malware Turns ScreenConnect Support Sessions Into Potential MSP Attack Paths
stories.abstract: Attackers are leveraging a critical vulnerability in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to deploy the SCKit malware. This campaign targets remote access sessions, allowing unauthorized actors to establish persistent control over managed service provider environments through previously identified security gaps.
stories.why: Exploitation of remote management tools provides adversaries with high-level access to downstream client networks, facilitating widespread supply chain compromise.
stories.action: Ensure all ScreenConnect instances are updated to the latest patched version.

stories.title: TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
stories.abstract: TSMC confirmed a data breach involving employee information after a threat actor attempted to auction nearly 7GB of stolen files. The company identified a third-party cloud service provider as the entry point for the unauthorized access.
stories.why: Supply chain vulnerabilities remain a critical vector for large enterprises, demonstrating that third-party access can bypass internal security controls.

stories.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
stories.abstract: Cursor confirmed that attackers compromised its marketplace to distribute a malicious Claude Code extension. The breach originated from stolen credentials belonging to Fireworks AI, which allowed unauthorized access to Cursor's systems.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting developer tools and AI infrastructure can lead to widespread code injection and credential theft within development environments.

stories.title: YARA-X 1.23.0 Release, (Sun, Nov 15th)
stories.abstract: The YARA-X project has released version 1.23.0, which introduces four functional enhancements and addresses sixteen identified bugs to improve overall stability and performance.
stories.why: Security teams relying on YARA-X for malware detection and threat hunting should update to ensure consistent rule evaluation and avoid potential processing errors.

stories.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
stories.abstract: A researcher released a proof-of-concept exploit dubbed SignDrop that allows local users to escalate privileges to SYSTEM level on Windows systems. The vulnerability stems from how the operating system handles signature verification, potentially enabling unauthorized administrative control.
stories.why: Local privilege escalation flaws allow attackers who have already gained a foothold to achieve full system compromise and bypass security boundaries.

stories.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent
stories.abstract: Italian regulators fined Meta 805 million euros for violating privacy laws within its Android Facebook application. The platform automatically accessed user photo galleries and metadata to suggest content without obtaining the necessary informed consent required by local data protection authorities.
stories.why: This highlights the legal risks of aggressive data collection practices and the importance of explicit user authorization for accessing sensitive device storage.

stories.title: Check Point warns of zero-day flaw exploited for root access
stories.abstract: Check Point has issued emergency patches for a critical vulnerability affecting its Security Gateway products. Attackers have been actively exploiting this flaw since late October to obtain root-level access and maintain persistent control over compromised network appliances.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to gain full administrative control, posing a severe risk to perimeter security and internal network integrity.
stories.action: Apply the emergency hotfixes provided by Check Point immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Check Point Gateways to Deploy TSGA Backdoor and Wipe ESXi Files
stories.abstract: Threat actors are exploiting unpatched Check Point Security Gateways to gain initial access via PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. Attackers subsequently leveraged a local privilege escalation flaw in the Gaia OS to install a backdoor and deploy data-wiping malware targeting VMware ESXi environments.
stories.why: The campaign demonstrates a sophisticated pivot from network edge devices to hypervisor-level destruction, posing a severe risk to virtualized infrastructure integrity.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches provided by Check Point for Gaia OS and gateway appliances.

stories.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
stories.abstract: A state-sponsored threat actor dubbed SilentAir has compromised telecommunications infrastructure across Asia. By infiltrating network nodes, the group intercepted SMS and voice traffic, specifically targeting individuals in Taiwan. The campaign shares operational similarities with the previously identified Liminal Panda group.
stories.why: This highlights critical vulnerabilities in mobile network infrastructure and the persistent threat of state-level actors compromising telecom providers for targeted surveillance.

stories.title: Citrix Patches 12 NetScaler and Secure Access Client Flaws, Including Authentication Bypass
stories.abstract: Citrix released patches addressing 28 vulnerabilities across NetScaler ADC, Gateway, and Console, including a critical memory overflow flaw (CVE-2026-120868) that could trigger denial-of-service conditions. Secure Access clients for Linux and Windows also received updates to resolve related security issues.
stories.why: Critical memory flaws in edge infrastructure like NetScaler can lead to service outages or potential authentication bypasses if exploited.
stories.action: Update NetScaler ADC, Gateway, Console, and Secure Access clients to the latest versions immediately.

stories.title: Craft CMS security advisory (AV26-1086) - Update 1
stories.abstract: Craft CMS has released security updates to address multiple vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-123488, which is currently being exploited in the wild. Affected versions include CMS versions prior to 4.18.9 and 5.11.2, as well as the Commerce-mollie plugin prior to 4.4.3.
stories.why: Active exploitation of a CMS vulnerability poses a significant risk of unauthorized access or remote code execution on web infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Craft CMS to 4.18.9 or 5.11.2 and Commerce-mollie to 4.4.3 immediately.

stories.title: N-able security advisory (AV26-1143)
stories.abstract: N-able has released a security update for its N-central platform to address CVE-2026-125883. Reports indicate that this vulnerability is currently being exploited in the wild. Administrators must ensure their installations are running version 2026.4.1.26 or later to mitigate the risk.
stories.why: The vulnerability is confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing a significant risk to organizations utilizing N-central for remote management.
stories.action: Update N-central to version 2026.4.1.26 or newer immediately.

stories.title: FBI Says North Korean Hackers Stole Over $400 Million in Crypto Using Deepfake Video Calls
stories.abstract: The U.S. government has dismantled a North Korean social engineering operation known as FaceStealer. Over the past year and a half, the campaign successfully targeted victims to siphon more than $400 million in cryptocurrency assets.
stories.why: It highlights the sophisticated use of social engineering by state-sponsored actors to facilitate large-scale financial theft and money laundering.

stories.title: n8n security advisory (AV26-1160)
stories.abstract: The Canadian Cyber Centre has issued advisories for three distinct products: n8n workflow automation software, Apache HTTP Server, and Johnson Controls EasyIO firmware. Each platform contains security vulnerabilities requiring administrative attention to mitigate potential exploitation risks.
stories.why: These updates address critical flaws, including an OAuth account hijacking vulnerability in n8n and potential remote code execution risks in Apache HTTP Server.
stories.action: Update n8n to 3.0.1 or later, Apache HTTP Server to 2.4.71, and patch EasyIO firmware.

stories.title: No Signs of Hacking in FAA Ground Stop as FBI Reportedly Probes Software Update
stories.abstract: Federal authorities have found no evidence of a cyberattack regarding the recent nationwide FAA ground stop. Preliminary investigations suggest the operational disruption likely stemmed from a faulty software update rather than malicious external interference.
stories.why: Systemic failures in critical infrastructure often trigger security concerns; confirming a non-malicious root cause helps distinguish operational risk from targeted cyber threats.

stories.title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access
stories.abstract: A new proof-of-concept exploit dubbed SignDrop targets the Windows Common Log File System driver. By manipulating path redirection during log-authentication processes, local attackers can escalate privileges to SYSTEM level, bypassing security features introduced in the driver last year.
stories.why: Local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in core Windows drivers provide attackers with full system control, facilitating persistence and lateral movement within compromised environments.

stories.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE
stories.abstract: PostgreSQL released updates addressing 52 vulnerabilities, most notably a high-severity type confusion bug, CVE-2026-6460. This flaw allows authenticated users with object-creation privileges to execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with the database process's system permissions.
stories.why: Authenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities in database infrastructure pose a critical risk for lateral movement and full system compromise.
stories.action: Update PostgreSQL and rebuild all installed C-language extensions.

stories.title: This Comic Kills Technofascists
stories.abstract: A new action thriller titled Exploit has been released, focusing on the ongoing conflict between independent journalism and major technology corporations.

stories.title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
stories.abstract: While fully autonomous ransomware remains theoretical, low-skill threat actors are increasingly leveraging generative AI to enhance their operations. These tools lower the barrier to entry, allowing less experienced criminals to execute more effective and frequent attacks.
stories.why: AI lowers the technical threshold for cyberattacks, potentially increasing the volume and sophistication of ransomware campaigns targeting enterprise environments.

stories.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
stories.abstract: Threat actors hijacked nearly 5,000 GitHub accounts to inject malicious code into thousands of repositories. The campaign, known as wfx-loot, uses automated pull requests to deploy secret-stealing malware designed to harvest cloud credentials and sensitive environment variables from CI/CD workflows.
stories.why: Compromised CI/CD pipelines provide attackers with direct access to production cloud environments and sensitive infrastructure secrets.
stories.action: Audit CI/CD logs for unauthorized pull requests and rotate all secrets exposed in affected repositories.
